hook
In the heart of Baku, in the Old City, a tower has stood for centuries: the Maiden Tower. Who built it, when, and why? To this day, there is no definitive answer.
plan
In this video, we'll look at the legends and the historical evidence separately. And at the end, we'll decide together which version is more convincing.
facts

First, the numbers. The tower is about twenty-nine and a half meters tall, with a base diameter of sixteen and a half meters. Its walls are five meters thick at the bottom, and thin to three or four meters at the top. The tower has eight floors.
leg0
Part one: the legends. Around twenty legends are told about the Maiden Tower.
leg1

The most famous one goes like this: a ruler wants to marry his daughter to a man she does not love. To buy time, she asks her father to first build her a tall tower. When the tower is finished, she climbs to the top and throws herself down.
leg2

Another legend tells of a siege. When enemies surround Baku, a girl with fiery hair takes up a sword, defeats the enemy commander, and saves the city. This legend has roots in ancient Zoroastrian beliefs.
leg3
These stories also found their way into art. In nineteen forty, Afrasiyab Badalbeyli wrote the ballet Maiden Tower. It was the first Azerbaijani ballet.
ev0
Part two: the historical evidence. Legends are fascinating, but historians look at stones and records.
ev1

On the tower's south wall, about fourteen meters up, there is an inscription in Kufic script. It names Masud ibn Davud, and it is dated to the twelfth century. But the inscription does not clearly say that he was the tower's architect.
ev2

Some scholars believe the tower is much older. Davud Akhundov considered it a Zoroastrian fire temple, and dated it to the eighth or seventh century BC. Sara Ashurbeyli argued that the foundation and lower floors were built between the fourth and sixth centuries AD.
ev3

Excavations in nineteen sixty-two and sixty-three showed that the tower stands on a rock that slopes toward the sea. Inside, on the second floor, a well twenty-one meters deep was found. Ceramic pipes channeled rainwater into this well.
ev4
Another hypothesis says the tower was an ancient observatory. The reason: the long buttress attached to the tower faces east, toward the sunrise. But this idea has not been proven either.
today

Today, the Maiden Tower is a museum. In two thousand, the Old City of Baku, together with the Shirvanshahs' Palace and the Maiden Tower, was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List. The tower also appears on the ten manat banknote.
end

So what is the real secret? The most widely accepted view is that most of the building dates to the twelfth century. But the theory of more ancient roots is still being debated. Which version do you believe? Tell us in the comments. And don't forget to like the video and subscribe to the channel!
